source.title: Restoring grokking under structured label noise: audit efficiency and optimization-history dependence

record.file_problem: The full article is present and matches the supplied title, but its internal DOI is 10.64336/001c.163699, not the supplied ID.
record.tranche_reason: It tests delayed generalization on modular addition using grokking outcomes, but changes the training conditions through label noise, auditing, and mid-training correction rather than reproducing the original training setup.
record.gate_note: The article's own grokking and test-accuracy outcomes are recorded. Statements in the introduction and background about prior work, Fourier mechanisms, and other cited findings are not rows. Audit hit rates and correction rates are excluded because they measure audit efficiency, not grokking behavior.
record.test_reason: The study trains a two-layer MLP on modular addition (p=97). It reports whether and when test accuracy reaches the grokking criterion under clean labels and under 4% label noise, which bears on V1 in a new setting (label noise). Most of the paper compares audit policies and measures a hysteresis effect; neither is what any version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors' headline is that grokking recovery is path-dependent: continuing after correction is 10–16k epochs faster than reinitializing, and they do not isolate weights from optimizer state. They also conclude that both noise types at η=0.04 equally suppress grokking, that loss/entropy triage is the only policy that reliably restores it, and that which corruptions are fixed matters more than how many.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition and test-accuracy grokking criteria, but studies structured label noise, auditing, and temporal correction with a two-layer MLP rather than reproducing the original clean-training setup. It does not test training-set-size effects.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery outcome varies with noise rate, noise type, audit policy and budget, and whether optimization state is retained after correction. Clean-to-noisy persistence also differs by seed.

fits_no_version.finding: After labels are corrected at epoch 50k, continuing training from the existing weights and optimizer state groks 10–16k epochs sooner than reinitializing on the same data, in all 6 seed–noise runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking recovery after label correction depends on optimization history (hysteresis).

fits_no_version.finding: A grokked solution partly persists after 4% noise is injected (test accuracy 0.76–0.80). A run that had not consolidated collapses to about 0.43.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness of a grokked solution to later label noise depends on how consolidated it was.

fits_no_version.finding: Which corrupted labels are fixed matters more than how many. Loss/entropy triage restores grokking while region audit at an equal correction count does not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking under label noise is blocked by a specific subset of high-loss corruptions.

record.problems: Only modular addition with one stated architecture and fixed hyperparameters is tested. Experiments use three seeds. The temporal comparison changes weights, representations, and optimizer statistics together, so their individual contributions are not separated. Training-accuracy trajectories and training-set-size dependence are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: Audit hit-rate and correction-rate results were excluded because they measure auditing efficiency rather than grokking outcomes. Prior-work results cited in the introduction and background were not recorded as this study's results.

untested.parts: Training-accuracy saturation before the test jump, a chance-level start, and growth of the delay as the training set shrinks (n_train fixed at 5,000).
All. No circuit or progress measures are reported.
All. Only modular addition is used, with no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
All. Weight decay is fixed and there is no dataset-size sweep.
All. AdamW and float32 are fixed, with no optimizer or numerical controls.

missing.what: No-audit (and random-audit) outcomes at η=0.01. The text implies even 1% noise blocked grokking, since only loss audit 'restored' it. This is a stronger scope limit for V1 than the η=0.04 rows.
Region audit leaving about 69 of 200 corruptions (about 1.4% noise) still did not grok (final test ≈0.656). This shows residual noise below 2% suppresses grokking.
Condition D (clean retraining from scratch after correction) grokked about 38–46k epochs after restart, matching the clean baseline. This acts as an additional clean replication.

record.verdict_notes: The internal DOI is 10.64336/001c.163699, not the supplied ID. This is a high-school journal paper with three seeds, one architecture and fixed hyperparameters. Rows on audit policies and hysteresis were moved to 'none' because they evaluate the study's own method or a construct no version names. The tranche changes from T2 to T3: the new setting is label noise, and the clean baseline is a configuration check, not a replication of the original method.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report training-accuracy trajectories or test a training-set-size sweep, so it does not test whether training accuracy saturates first or whether delay grows as the training set shrinks.
No gradual circuit-formation or memorizing-component-removal measures are reported; the cited mechanistic findings are from prior work.
Only modular addition is tested; no non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm manipulation is reported.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
Weight decay is held fixed. The study does not test whether low norm selects an efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
No identifiable algorithms are compared across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
The study reports using float32 but does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or softmax numerical limits, nor compare controlled optimizer or numerical settings.
